topic.title: Clarification on Rule 2.6: publicly shared generated passages and API-generated training data
topic.author: Clivin John

raw.title: Clarification on Rule 2.6: publicly shared generated passages and API-generated training data
Clarification on Rule 2.6: publicly shared generated passages and API-generated training data

firstMessage.content:
Hi hosts,

Several top public notebooks pretrain on a pool of ~35k passages merged from community Kaggle datasets, where participants generated text from the competition’s 18 models via APIs/proxies. Could you clarify:

  • Is training on these already-published community datasets (CC BY / CC BY-SA) permitted for prize-eligible solutions?
  • Is generating additional passages via paid APIs permitted, and if so, what cost level counts as “reasonable” under Section 2.6?
  • If such data is allowed, does it need to be publicly shared before a certain date (e.g. the entry deadline) to be used in final submissions?
  • A participant reported that Gemini 3.7 Flash requests were routed to 3.8 after 8 October. Can you confirm whether the competition’s 3.7 labels were generated before any such change?

Thanks. A clear answer would help a lot of teams avoid building on data that may later be ruled out.
